A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Token Distillation research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original biomedical and French benchmark evaluations, definition-generation experiments, ablations, and initialization-runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds compression-oriented French and Arabic experiments, continued-training comparisons, and downstream timing measurements.

M1.justification: The hidden-state distillation objective, alignment procedure, frozen-model initialization, and optional NTP combinations remain unchanged. Isolated and joint optimization were already described in v2. The added continued-training experiments evaluate the existing initializer rather than introduce a new distillation component.

E1.justification: v3 retains the earlier coverage and adds Arabic multiple-choice evaluation through arabic_leaderboard_light and Arabic FineWeb-2 documents for timing. Section 5.2 also extends evaluation from whole-word French tokens to compression-selected tokens that can include ambiguous subwords, substantially broadening the tested token population.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments, including the retained appendix comparisons with Tokens to Words. The new experiments reuse subtoken Mean, NTP, and original-tokenization controls. AdaptiVocab supplies token selection and a shared adaptation protocol rather than a new competing initialization method.

E3.justification: Existing protocols are retained, but the added experiments use 100 rather than 25 snippets per token and new compression-oriented token configurations. Arabic evaluation adds 1,000 steps of continued training of embeddings and the first and last Transformer layers. Appendix B.4 introduces forward-only and forward/backward timing on 8,192 documents with hardware-specific batch sizes.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds an initialization-only versus continued-training comparison, testing whether initialization advantages persist after vocabulary adaptation. Appendix B.4 adds empirical analysis of whether token-count reductions translate into runtime savings on H100 and B200 GPUs. The earlier objective, target-layer, initialization, context-source, and two-epoch analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2's blanket five-seed statement for stochastic methods is removed; v3 explicitly specifies five seeds in the biomedical table captions instead. Standard deviations, Bonferroni-corrected Welch tests, and stated single-seed exceptions remain unchanged. This narrows the reporting scope without establishing any change in actual run counts.

E6.justification: All eleven earlier tables retain their result values after matching renumbered tables. New Tables 4–5 report French and Arabic compression results; Arabic Token Distillation scores 44.2 without and 47.5 with continued training. Table 12 newly reports forward-runtime reductions of 41.7% on H100 and 49.7% on B200. These are added results under new conditions, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, alignment mapping, Equation 1, and loss-autoscaling rule are equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced; the added quadratic-attention explanation is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: distilling contextual representations yields high-quality input embeddings and outperforms the evaluated initialization baselines. The new experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations concerning ambiguous compression-selected tokens and hypothesizes that over-fragmentation limits Arabic continued-training benefits. Appendix C.9 qualifies the preference for joint optimization when many input embeddings are new, and Section 5.3 suggests mapping-based initialization for low lexical overlap. Most existing limitations are simply relocated.

D1.justification: v3 adds Arabic evaluation commands, continued-training hyperparameters, and timing hardware and processing details. It newly states approximately 11,600 French whole-word tokens, adds task-configuration paths, and changes the code/version-lockfile disclosure from promised to available. These extend documentation without revising the existing initialization implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Elfilali et al. (2024) for Arabic evaluation and expands the experimental role of the already cited AdaptiVocab. It removes Minixhofer et al. (2025) and the discussion of concurrent cross-tokenizer distillation. The broader positioning against embedding aggregation, NTP, and hyper-networks remains.

P1.justification: v3 inserts Section 5.2, moves limitations to Appendix A, and reorganizes appendix subsections. Most existing prose remains intact, with localized terminology and sentence corrections, including clarification of the previously confusing NTP comparison and updated publication headers.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4–5 side by side and Table 12, and moves the distillation-objective table from the main text to Appendix B.1. Captions, labels, and placement receive limited revisions. All three figure graphics and the basic formatting of retained tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens practical validation through compression-selected tokens, the continued-training comparison, and measured downstream speedups (Tables 4–5 and 12), while preserving the earlier evidence. The new performance comparisons lack uncertainty estimates, and removing the concurrent-distillation discussion slightly weakens research positioning. The added evidence provides a positive but limited overall quality improvement.
